thread_text:
incident-bot: 🔔 Paging: P1 - high request latency for inference-service (us-west-2). Pager: Maya. Incident page: https://incidents.redwood.ai/2390012345 — affected customers: ~12. Severity: degraded latency.
Maya: On it, joining now.
Maya: Quick symptom: tail latency 90p/95p/99p spike, p99 > 3s, error rate stable. Traffic volume normal.
Sophia: Looking at Grafana — KV cache evictions spike around the same time, hit ratio dropped ~35%.
Tom: Tried a quick pool restart, no meaningful change. Re-routing a slice to model:v2-small to test latency impact: `/control reroute inference-service us-west-2 model=v2-small 10%`
Maya: Rolled 10% -> v2-small, p90 improved immediately, p99 partially better. Customers A & B reported slower responses earlier but no request failures persisted. ETA to observe 10m.
incident-bot: Handoff requested: Maya -> Liam at +20m. Please ack.
Liam: taking over for monitoring. Maya — any runbook links or notes?
Maya: Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.ai/inference/high-latency. Key notes: KV cache thundering on cold-population, some autoscaler throttles in us-west-2. Tried pool restart, partial route to v2-small.
Liam: Confirming error rate steady. If it's only latency, I propose temporarily relaxing the paging noise threshold to 4s for 30m while we stabilize. Thoughts?
Rachel: Please don't globally relax the alert threshold — that masks regressions. Instead add an alert suppression for the warmed-up instances and create a dashboard panel broken down by model variant/zone so we can see where p99 is concentrated.
Jenna: I'll spin up a targeted Grafana panel: p95/p99/p999 by model+availability_zone, with a drilldown link to traces. Example query I'll use: 
```
avg_over_time(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, zone))[5m:1m])
```
This will get us p99 per model/zone.
Sophia: Agree on golden signals: p99 latency, error_rate, throughput. Also add KV cache hit ratio as a first-class metric for this service.
Tom: Filed infra ticket INFR-4521 for alert tuning + dashboard work, assigned to Jenna + eng-oncall.
Liam: Customer impact summary so far: ~12 customers experienced degraded latency, median extra latency ~1.8s, 3 customers saw transient client timeouts (retries recovered). No data loss. Will include in postmortem.
Maya: Closing the page for now — traffic to v2-small reduced tail latency. Continue monitoring. Retro scheduled tomorrow 10:00am PT. Action items: 1) new Grafana panels + drilldowns, 2) alert modifications to be model-aware, 3) bake cache prewarm in autoscaler, 4) follow-up runbook updates.
Jenna: Starting dashboard PR — repo: https://git.redwood.ai/grafana/dashboards — PR: https://git.redwood.ai/grafana/pulls/78. Panel config snippet I'm adding: 
```json
{"panel": {"title": "Inference p99 by model/zone", "targets": [{"expr": "histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, zone))"}]}}
```
Liam: Perfect — include a panel-level drilldown URL to traces and the runbook. Also add alert rule that tags alerts with `model` label so oncall can route faster.
GrafanaBot: Dashboard created: grafana/inference/incident-retro-panel by Jenna.
Rachel: For the post-incident alert tuning, let's do a short experiment window (48h) after dashboard merges: add temporary suppression for synthetic warmups, but keep model-scoped thresholds so we don't blind ourselves.
Jenna: Noted. I'll include a proposed alert change in the PR description and a test dashboard for the suppression rules.
Liam: I'll write the incident summary and attach the dashboard PR + graphs in the retro doc. Thanks all.
Maya: :thumbsup: great work.
incident-bot: Incident 2390012345 marked resolved (mitigated) by Maya. Postmortem assignment: Maya (lead), Liam (ops), Jenna (dashboards).
Liam: Leaving a follow-up checklist in the postmortem: add model-aware alerts, KV-hit ratio panel, autoscaler prewarm experiment, and runbook update with traffic reroute steps.
Jenna: I'll merge PR after tests and post the dashboard link to the retro doc.
Maya: closing channel thread — see you at the retro. :white_check_mark:
